# AE-app

AE-app, the A&E Tracker, provides interactive analysis of time series data on
accident and emergency department attendances. A live instance of the app is
[here](https://clahrcnwl.shinyapps.io/ae-app/).

The app uses Shewhart charts, drawn with
[autospc](https://github.com/HorridTom/autospc), to analyse the percentage of
attendances where the patient was admitted, transferred or discharged within
four hours of arrival, and the average daily numbers of attendances and of
emergency admissions. It does this for publicly available
[NHS England](https://www.england.nhs.uk/statistics/statistical-work-areas/ae-waiting-times-and-activity/)
and [Public Health Scotland](https://www.opendata.nhs.scot/dataset/weekly-accident-and-emergency-activity-and-waiting-times)
data, nationally, by region or health board, and by provider or hospital.

More details on the methods used are in the "Understanding the analysis" tab of
the app.

## Data

The app reads its data from the [AE-data](https://github.com/HorridTom/AE-data)
repository, where a scheduled GitHub Action updates it every week using
[nhsAEscraper](https://github.com/HorridTom/nhsAEscraper). (Until 2025 the data
was held in a MySQL database on AWS.) The app reads the data once, when it
starts, so a running copy picks up new data when it next restarts.

Contains public sector information licensed under the
[Open Government Licence v3.0](https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3/).

## Run the app locally

The package versions the app uses are recorded with
[renv](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/). After cloning this repo, open the
project and run:

``` r
renv::restore()
shiny::runApp()
```

This needs an internet connection to download the data. To use a local copy of
the AE-data repository instead:

``` r
Sys.setenv(AE_DATA_SOURCE = "~/Rprojects/AE-data/data")
shiny::runApp()
```

## Code

`app.R` loads the data and starts the app. The functions it uses are in `R/`,
which Shiny loads automatically:

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `data_loading.R` | Reading the data from AE-data |
| `data_preparation.R` | Putting England's and Scotland's data in one format; looking up organisations |
| `series.R` | `make_series()`: the time series for one organisation |
| `charts.R` | `chart_performance()` and `chart_volume()`: the Shewhart charts |
| `app_ui.R`, `app_server.R` | The app's layout, and its responses to the user's choices |
| `chart_module.R` | A chart with its download button |
| `ui_text.R` | Text of the "Understanding the analysis" and "Development" tabs |

## Tests

``` r
shiny::runTests()
```

The test data in `tests/testthat/test-data` is made by
`tests/testthat/make_test_data.R`.

## Deploy

The app is hosted on [shinyapps.io](https://www.shinyapps.io/) (account
`clahrcnwl`). With the account connected in RStudio
(`rsconnect::setAccountInfo()`), deploy with:

``` r
rsconnect::deployApp(appName = "ae-app", account = "clahrcnwl")
```

## Example analyses

Example charts for the whole of England.

```{r england, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
library(stringr)
shiny::loadSupport(".", renv = environment())

ae_data <- prepare_ae_data(read_ae_file("England"), read_ae_file("Scotland"))
england <- make_series(ae_data, "National", "E", only_reporting = TRUE)

chart_performance(england, "National", only_reporting = TRUE)
chart_volume(england, "National", only_reporting = TRUE)
```
